Working notes:

- Intake forms have two schemas:
  - Version 1 fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
  - Version 2 fields: cust, date, email, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Source records may label equivalent fields differently: customer -> cust; quantity -> qty. Preserve the form’s date field name (order_date for v1, date for v2).
- Validate every required field, especially priority and ship_country. These were the most frequent rejection causes; qty was also rejected on v1 records.
- Do not assume reception/intake notes such as “ordinary priority,” partner-portal origin, or duplicate checks make fields valid.
- Version 2 records can be accepted when all fields are correctly populated: ORD-5110 and ORD-5115 succeeded. A version 2 record with invalid priority/ship_country was rejected despite having otherwise complete data.
- Retry limits matter: attempts are explicitly tracked (up to 3). After the final failed attempt, stop processing and send the record to manual review.
- For retries, correct only confirmed invalid fields and retain valid customer, email, date, and quantity values.

Working notes:

- Intake schemas observed:
  - Version 1: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
  - Versions 2, 3, and 4: cust, date, email, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Map source labels consistently: customer -> cust; quantity -> qty. Preserve the form’s date field name.
- Validate every required field strictly, especially priority and ship_country. Invalid priority/ship_country repeatedly caused rejection, regardless of notes claiming “ordinary priority,” completed duplicate checks, or partner-portal origin.
- Validate qty as well; it was rejected on v1, v3, and v4 records. Do not infer validity from an apparently plausible source value.
- Unexpected fields can be invalid: status was explicitly rejected on a version 3 record. Submit only fields in the selected schema.
- Versions 2 and 3 have accepted records; version 4 has so far shown rejection, not evidence that its schema differs. Treat versions 3 and 4 as using the same six-field schema unless new evidence appears.
- For retries, correct only confirmed invalid fields and retain valid cust, email, date, and quantity values. A version 3 record was accepted on attempt 3 after correction, confirming retries can succeed.
- Attempts are explicitly tracked, up to 3. After the final failed attempt, stop processing and route the record to manual review; do not make another submission.
- Reception/intake comments and duplicate-check claims do not substitute for valid field values.
